container_environment.middle: the presence and equality template, then one container ID

render.middle: --project-name, --env-file and the signed -f list, the override on standard input as the last file

verify.middle: read-only binds of signed directories, the signed image ID, python -I -B -

file_contents_read: the one regular file the request names, to compare it with the signed hash

lock.kind: flock on a descriptor opened read-only and without following a link; the file is never created, written or removed
lock.probe: a shared, non-blocking request released at once: it fails only while another process holds the lock exclusively; for that instant a non-blocking exclusive request of another process fails as well
lock.released: explicitly, and in any case when the process ends

never: a container with a bind it can write through
a network connection opened by this process
side_effects: one attached docker run --rm: the engine creates a container and removes it when its process ends; a run that times out may leave it running until then
a shared, non-blocking flock on the deployment lock, released at once
docker compose config reads the environment file; its values stay in the memory of this process and never reach the receipt
scope.statement: Demonstration only; never bound. Reads and changes nothing on the filesystem of the host: signed directories, image and container metadata, the signed environment names of one container as booleans, one regular file compared with a signed hash, a compose render, and whether the deployment lock is free. It creates and removes one container that has no network and only read-only binds.
